newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to seek less foreign credit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to seek less foreign credit in 1997.

text.p: Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said the Colombian government will seek to reduce it dependency on foreign credit in 1997.

"The government has made a commitment with the central bank board to revise its foreign debt program for 1997," Ocampo told reporters, adding that the goal was "to make less use of foreign indebtedness next year."
Ocampo, who spoke after closed-door talks with the central bank's policy-making board of directors, declined further comment, saying details would be announced within the next two weeks.
The government, whose foreign debt is expected to total $16.19 billion by year-end, has raised $1.38 billion through sovereign debt issues so far this year.

A senior finance ministry official said recently that the government was planning to tap international bond markets for an additional $1.8 billion in financing in 1997 but that figure could be subject to change, in light of Ocampo's announcement.
